hyps.why: Node 2 only reaches the output through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed any op on edge 1 is irrelevant.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which is disconnected from the output when edge 5 is none.
With edge 4 removed, node 1's features reach the output only indirectly via edges 2 and 5, diluting the edit's impact.
Without the direct input-output edge the node-2 path carries more of the signal, so a strong conv there matters more.
When edge 5 is cut the direct edge becomes a critical path, so making it a 3x3 conv yields a larger gain.
Removing edge 3 when edge 4 is already absent leaves only edge 5 into the output, risking a near-disconnected cell.
Cutting edge 5 when edge 3 is absent leaves at most edge 4 feeding the output, sharply hurting accuracy.
With edge 1 removed node 2 depends only on edge 2, so the conv on edge 5 often processes a weak or zero signal.
Replacing an existing 1x1 conv with a 3x3 conv gives a much smaller gain than replacing none, skip or pooling.
Filling an empty edge with a 3x3 conv adds a new learnable path, a larger gain than swapping out an existing operation.
